first.rationale: Two of the three current problems are funnel-mechanics problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%), and the inherited record points directly at those mechanics: memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (fewer signup fields lifted SMB first-week activation), with memory_91 as a close second-best lever on the activation half. Fixing the funnel addresses the observed regressions and is the path most consistent with sustainable long-term qualified revenue, whereas promotional pricing (memory_73) is the option the competitive shock is pushing me toward emotionally and is the one whose 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' most plausibly hides downstream value risk: discount-acquired price-sensitive SMBs can raise headline revenue while lowering retention, expansion, and lifetime qualified value, and the summary as consolidated says nothing about the horizon over which lift was measured. That is exactly why I am spending my two verification pulls on memory_86 (the load-bearing claim under my intended action, to check whether the original record measured completion only or also downstream revenue quality, and on which segment) and memory_73 (the strongest rival under situational pressure, to check retention and margin effects and measurement window before I rule it out). memory_31 is old (day 12) and overlaps memory_86, so it is corroborating rather than decisive; memory_57 and memory_44 target segments that are not where the current bleeding is. Caveats I am carrying forward rather than discarding: these are consolidated summaries whose originals I have not yet read, all of them predate the competitor's entry pricing so the environment they were learned in may no longer hold, and simplifying signup can itself degrade lead qualification data and admit lower-quality accounts, which would trade activation gains against qualified revenue. So I run this as a standard experiment with a holdout, and I instrument downstream qualified-revenue and retention proxies, not just completion and activation rates. If the memory_86 archive reveals the lift was completion-only with no revenue-quality evidence, or if memory_73 turns out to have clean long-horizon retention data, I will revise before committing the slot.
